Since $g: \mathbb{Z} \to O$ (odd integers), $g(5)$ and $g(-1)$ must be odd integers that sum to 6.
Possible pairs $(g(5), g(-1))$ include $(1, 5)$, $(3, 3)$, $(5, 1)$, $(-1, 7)$, etc.

We select the simplest solution where $g(5) = g(-1) = 3$, as this is a common pattern in such problems.

    $$g(15) + g(9) = 6$$
    Using the derived fact $g(9)=9$:

This result, $g(15)=-3$, is an odd integer, satisfying the domain constraint $g:\mathbb{Z}\to O$.
